clinician.trajectory_summary: A 64-year-old man with prior IgG4 lung disease (diagnosed 16 months earlier by lung biopsy) and documented positive c-ANCA (1:160) with PR3 antibody (15) presented to rheumatology clinic with 3 weeks of progressive productive cough, haemoptysis, myalgias, arthralgias, weakness, and 2-3 days of fever and chills. Chest CT on admission showed marked interval increase in diffuse lung opacities with some coalesced nodules and masses. Bronchoscopy revealed copious blood in the right main stem bronchus and right middle lobe, confirming pulmonary hemorrhage and necessitating intubation for hypoxic respiratory failure. Renal biopsy was performed on admission. The patient was treated with intravenous methylprednisolone (1 g/day for 3 days), monthly intravenous cyclophosphamide, and seven cycles of plasmapheresis. He required hemodialysis but was extubated after 2 weeks and discharged after 1 month on home oxygen. One month post-discharge, he was significantly improved with creatinine of 3.6 mg/dL and no longer requiring dialysis. The diagnosis of GPA was established on the basis of renal biopsy, pulmonary hemorrhage, and high-titer PR3-ANCA antibodies.

High-titer PR3-ANCA antibodies (PR3 antibody 15, c-ANCA 1:160) documented at baseline
Renal biopsy performed on admission establishing GPA diagnosis
Treatment response to immunosuppression (methylprednisolone, cyclophosphamide, plasmapheresis) with clinical improvement and renal recovery
Hypoxic respiratory failure requiring intubation following bronchoscopy with pulmonary hemorrhage

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: While patient had prior IgG4 lung disease diagnosis 16 months ago, the acute presentation with pulmonary hemorrhage, renal involvement, high-titer PR3-ANCA, and response to ANCA-associated vasculitis treatment (cyclophosphamide, plasmapheresis) indicates evolution to or concurrent GPA rather than isolated IgG4 disease

Broad-spectrum antibiotics were begun for presumed infection, but the clinical course, renal biopsy findings, and response to immunosuppression rather than antibiotics support vasculitis rather than infection

remaining_uncertainties: Specific histopathological findings from renal biopsy (crescents, necrotizing vasculitis, glomerular involvement, immunofluorescence pattern) - unable to retrieve due to system restrictions on diagnosis-revealing records
Urinalysis findings (hematuria, proteinuria, RBC casts) at presentation that prompted renal biopsy
Serum creatinine and renal function at time of presentation
Current PR3-ANCA titer at presentation and comparison to prior baseline (whether titer increased)
Histopathological features of original lung biopsy from 16 months ago (IgG4 features vs. early vasculitis features)
